newsitem.title: USA: Ariad, Hoechst Marion in venture.
newsitem.headline: Ariad, Hoechst Marion in venture.

text.p: Hoechst Marion Roussel and ARIAD Pharmaceuticals Inc, said Thursday they have reached an agreement to form a 50/50 joint venture to pursue functional genomics.
The companies said they have agreed to commit $85 million to the joint venture and its first five years of operations.
The joint venture will be called Hoechst-ARIAD Genomics Center LLC and will be based at ARIAD's research facilities in Cambridge Massachusetts, they said.

They said the center will use state-of-the-art technologies in molecular and cellular genetics and bioinformatics to analyze human genes and identify those genes that encode novel therapeutic proteins or targets for small-molecule drug discovery.
The closing of the deal is subject to the expiration of the waiting period under federal antitrust regulations and other closing conditions, they said.
As part of the joint venture agreement, Hoechst Marion agreed to buy 2.5 million shares of ARIAD series B convertible preferred stock for $24 million.
The preferred stock is convertible one-for-one into ARIAD common stock and represnets 12 percent of ARIAD's outstanding shares.

At ARIAD's option, Hoechst Marion will make additional purchases of the preferred stock totalling up to $25 million. The purchases are to be made under a pre-determined pricing formula but in no case will represent more than 1.8 million additional shares of ARIAD preferred shgares.
The stock purchase agreement includes provisions restricting the further purchase or sale by Hoechst Marion of ARAID stock for a period extending beyond the term of the joint venture.
In a related move, the companies said that ARIAD will buy a license to Incyte Pharmaceutical Inc's LifeSeq database and the joint venture will be added as an installation site.
Hoechst Marion, meanwhile, will extend an existing three-year subscription to the Incyte database to more than five years, they said.
